subject: Bancorp model evals & Redwood setup - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@bancorp.com>, Tom Rodriguez <tom.rodriguez@bancorp.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Bancorp model evals & Redwood setup - recap + next steps

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a small POC eval running on Redwood: 

Summary of needs:
- Primary use case: automated support summarization + answer retrieval for banking product docs (sensitive PII redaction required).
- Traffic profile: initial proof-of-concept ~50k tokens/day, target scale later.
- Key quality concerns: factuality on product terms, avoidance of hallucinations on regulatory language, response consistency across prompts.

Redwood recommendations (initial model shortlist):
- rw-instruct-2.7b (low-cost, fast baseline)
- rl-13b-q4 (balanced quality/cost; strong for instruction-following)
- open-7b-ctr (if strict latency needed)

What we propose for the eval run:
1) Run a customer-specific eval on Redwood using your sample dataset (attached). We'll run the three model variants above and compare: exact-match / token-level metrics, semantic-similarity (embedding-based), and a small human blind pass/fail set for critical cases.
2) Shared prompt set: see bancorp_eval_promptset_v1.csv (attached). We can iterate prompts after round 1.
3) Scoring criteria: — primary metric: strict answer correctness (domain-exact where applicable); — secondary: semantic similarity threshold >0.8; — safety filter failures must be 0 for PII.

Action items / ask from you:
- Confirm the sample dataset format is okay (CSV with id, prompt, expected_answer, category).
- Flag any regulatory wording we should treat as ground-truth exceptions.
- Confirm we can run evals on a test S3 bucket (we'll provide upload instructions).

Attachments: bancorp_eval_promptset_v1.csv (CSV of prompts/sample expected answers), redwood_eval_guide.pdf (short runbook)

I’ll get Dev to draft a short eval_config.yaml for the run and share an S3 path. Let us know a good time for a 30-min tech setup next week (we’re flexible).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

From: Tom Rodriguez <tom.rodriguez@bancorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@bancorp.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-16T09:15:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Bancorp model evals & Redwood setup - recap + next steps

Thanks Marissa — really useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Dataset: we can provide ~500 labeled examples for the POC in the CSV format you mention (id, prompt, expected_answer, category). We'll attach a small sample later today.
- PII: yes, PII must be redacted in the test data. For the human-eval set we can provide a de-identified subset with keys mapped.
- Regulatory exceptions: any explicit regulatory language in the "Disclosures" category should be considered ground truth; do not apply model paraphrase tolerances there.

A couple of asks for you: 
1) Can Redwood run per-token cost estimates for each model variant for our dataset size?
2) Do you support running a holdout A/B comparison where 10% of traffic is routed to an alternate config?

We'd like to schedule the tech setup for Tue 6/23 if that works.

Tom
Tom Rodriguez
Lead Product Manager, AI 
Bancorp

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Rodriguez <tom.rodriguez@bancorp.com>
Date: 2026-06-16T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Bancorp model evals & Redwood setup - recap + next steps

Thanks — adding technical details for the POC eval run so the team can prep.

Quick setup notes:
- Data format: CSV with columns [id, prompt, expected_answer, category, metadata_json(optional)]. Metadata JSON can include doc_id, source_url, and redaction_map.
- Upload: we'll give you an S3 pre-signed bucket by EOD. File size limit per upload: 200 MB.
- Eval config (summary):
    * models: ["rw-instruct-2.7b", "rl-13b-q4", "open-7b-ctr"]
    * metrics: exact_match_rate, normalized_levenshtein, embedding_similarity(avg), rouge_l, safety_flag_count
    * human_eval_sample: 50 items (blind) stratified across categories, scored pass/fail and severity
    * regression checks: baseline run against your control set; any drop >3% in exact_match triggers quality review

Recommended scoring thresholds for POC:
- Exact match >= 78% for core product Q&A categories
- Embedding similarity >= 0.82 for freeform paraphrase categories
- Safety filter failures = 0 for PII categories (fail immediate)

Deliverables from Redwood for this run:
- Detailed per-model metrics dashboard (token breakdowns, latency, cost estimate)
- Per-prompt failure logs and example traces (redacted)
- A short analysis note with recommended model & prompt adjustments after round 1

Attachments referenced: eval_config.yaml (we'll attach the YAML with exact keys).

Question for Bancorp: for the human-eval panel, do you have internal SME reviewers or should we recruit Redwood contract reviewers? SME reviewers preferred for domain accuracy.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwoodinference.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Rodriguez <tom.rodriguez@bancorp.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@bancorp.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-17T08:20:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Bancorp model evals & Redwood setup - recap + next steps

Perfect — thank you all. Next steps: 
- Tom / Sam: upload the sample CSV to the S3 link we'll share, or reply with files and we'll ingest.
- Dev: please push the eval_config.yaml to the Drive link and add estimated per-token costs for the three models based on 50k tokens/day.
- Neha: I'll follow up with a draft mutual action plan and an updated timeline for the 6/23 tech setup (30 min).

We’ll also prepare a short security one-pager (SOC2 scope, data handling) to address the PII handling questions in parallel.

Meeting: Tue 2026-06-23 10:00 AM EDT — 30 min tech setup (please confirm).

Attachments: redwood_eval_guide.pdf (shared)

Thanks — excited to get this running.

Marissa
